title: We’re Late, Felix
菲力克斯，我們晚了
paras: Felix Brandt, Rachel Gomez’s busiest {{client|client}}, walked into her office without an appointment, holding a tea infuser. “Someone is selling copies of my product,” he said, “under almost the same name.” Rachel had been the lawyer for his startup, Kettlebloom, since its first month, and she knew he had never registered anything. “I’ll be honest,” she said. “We’re late.”
菲力克斯・布蘭特是蕾秋・戈麥斯最忙的客戶，沒有預約就走進她的辦公室，手裡拿著一個泡茶器。「有人在賣我產品的仿冒品，」他說，「名稱還幾乎一模一樣。」蕾秋從他的新創公司 Kettlebloom 成立的第一個月起就擔任他們的律師，她知道他什麼都沒登記過。「我跟你說實話，」她說。「我們晚了。」

Kettlebloom had never been registered as a {{trademark|trademark}}, so nothing officially protected the name from the copycat. “Now the design,” she said. “Did you apply for a {{patent|patent}} on the infuser?” Felix looked at the floor. “I was going to.” Then Rachel pulled out his agreement with the freelancer who had drawn the logo. The {{copyright|copyright}} still belonged to the designer, because nobody had put a transfer in writing. “I’ll {{obtain|obtain}} a signed transfer from her tomorrow,” Rachel said. “She likes you. She’ll agree.”
Kettlebloom 從來沒有註冊成商標，所以沒有任何正式登記來保護這個名稱不被仿冒者使用。「接著是設計，」她說。「你有為這個泡茶器申請專利嗎？」菲力克斯低頭看著地板。「我本來打算要申請的。」接著蕾秋抽出他和繪製標誌的自由接案設計師簽的合約。著作權仍然屬於設計師，因為沒有人把轉讓的事寫成書面。「明天我會向她取得一份簽署好的轉讓書，」蕾秋說。「她喜歡你，會同意的。」

Within a week, Rachel had filed the trademark and patent applications and gotten the designer’s signature. Then she wrote to the marketplace to {{inquire|inquire}} about how to report copied products. Her letter was polite and firm. She {{enclose|enclosed}} the filing receipts and the signed transfer, and asked the marketplace to {{terminate|terminate}} the seller’s account if the listings stayed up. Two weeks later they were gone. Felix sent her flowers, and she sent him her bill.
一週內，蕾秋就送出了商標和專利兩項申請，也拿到了設計師的簽名。接著她寫信給網路商城，詢問如何檢舉仿冒商品。她的信措辭客氣但態度堅定。她隨信附上送件收據和簽署好的轉讓書，並要求商城如果那些商品頁面還掛著，就終止該賣家的帳號。兩週後，那些頁面全都不見了。菲力克斯送了她一束花，她則寄給他帳單。
